A)ZBPE ZLHW B)2606101600 C) PERM 
E) AIRCRAFT OPERATING ON THE THE FOLLOWING ROUTES SHALL ADHERE TO 
THE SPECIAL EMERGENCY DESCENT PROCEDURE. 
1.APPLICABLE ROUTES 
ROUTE W277, SEGMENT MUMOD-VARSO 
ROUTE W45, SEGMENT SADET-ATMIL 
ROUTE W276, SEGMENT ATMIL-BOVKI 
ROUTE B215, SEGMENT ADBES-OVKOM 
ROUTE W287, SEGMENT OVKOM-MENED 
ROUTE G212, SEGMENT WJC-TONOV 
2.SPECIAL PROCEDURE FOR EMERGENCY DESCENT 
2.1 IN AN EMERGENCY SITUATION THAT THREATENS FLIGHT SAFETY, THE 
PIC(PILOT IN COMMAND) HAS THE RIGHT TO CHANGE THE ORIGINALLY 
ASSIGNED FLIGHT LEVEL, BUT SHALL IMMEDIATELY REPORT TO THE ATC AND 
WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR THE ACTION TAKEN.THE SPECIAL PROCEDURE FOR 
EMERGENCY DESCENT SHALL BE: TURN RIGHT 30 DEGREES FROM THE 
AIRCRAFT'S CURRENT FLIGHT TRACK, MAINTAIN THE HEADING TO ESTABLISH 
A 5NM (9.3KM) OFFSET, THEN DESCEND TO THE NEW FLIGHT LEVEL AND 
TURN BACK TO THE ORIGINAL ROUTE BY ATC. 
2.2 IF THE AIRCRAFT IS UNABLE TO COMPLY WITH THE ABOVE 
REQUIREMENTS, THE PIC SHALL ESTABLISH CONTACT WITH ATC AS SOON AS 
POSSIBLE AND STATE 
 ) 
// // THE INTENTION. 
2.3 ONCE THE SAFETY THREAT HAS BEEN RESOLVED, THE PIC SHALL ADVISE 
ATC PROMPTLY IF REQUIRING RADAR VECTORS TO REJOIN THE ORIGINAL 
ROUTE. ATC SHALL CONTINUE TO PROVIDE AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES 
CONSIDERING CURRENT TRAFFIC FLOW, AIRSPACE STRUCTURE, 
METEOROLOGICAL CONDITIONS AND OTHER AIRSPACE USER ACTIVITIES. 
 ) 
// //

2.SPECIAL PROCEDURE FOR EMERGENCY DESCENT 
2.1 IN AN EMERGENCY SITUATION THAT THREATENS FLIGHT SAFETY, THE 
PIC(PILOT IN COMMAND) HAS THE RIGHT TO CHANGE THE ORIGINALLY 
ASSIGNED FLIGHT LEVEL, BUT SHALL IMMEDIATELY REPORT TO THE ATC AND 
WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR THE ACTION TAKEN.THE SPECIAL PROCEDURE FOR 
EMERGENCY DESCENT SHALL BE: TURN RIGHT 30 DEGREES FROM THE 
AIRCRAFT'S CURRENT FLIGHT TRACK, MAINTAIN THE HEADING TO ESTABLISH 
A 5NM (9.3KM) OFFSET, THEN DESCEND TO THE NEW FLIGHT LEVEL AND 
TURN BACK TO THE ORIGINAL ROUTE BY ATC. 
2.2 IF THE AIRCRAFT IS UNABLE TO COMPLY WITH THE ABOVE 
REQUIREMENTS, THE PIC SHALL ESTABLISH CONTACT WITH ATC AS SOON AS 
POSSIBLE AND STATE

1.IMPLEMENTATION WEATHER CONDITIONS 
1.1 VISUAL APPROACH MAY BE IMPLEMENTED WHEN THE PREVAILING 
VISIBILITY AT LISHE AIRPORT IS GREATER THAN 5 KM AND THE CLOUD 
BASE IS AT OR ABOVE 1,400 METERS. 
2. INSTRUCTIONS FOR PILOTS 
2.1 WHEN CONDITIONS PERMIT THE IMPLEMENTATION OF VISUAL APPROACH, 
ATC WILL NOTIFY PILOTS OF THE AVAILABLE APPROACH TYPE VIA ATIS. 
2.2 THE VISUAL APPROACH COULD BE APPLIED BY PILOT OR ATC, 
IMPLEMENTED AFTER APPROVED BY THE OTHER SIDE.ATC WILL INFORM THE 
FLIGHT CREW OF THE EXPECTED VISUAL APPROACH, IF THE FLIGHT CREW 
CANNOT ACCEPT THE VISUAL APPROACH, THE FLIGHT CREW MUST INFORM ATC 
IMMEDIATELY. 
2.3 ATC MAY ISSUE VISUAL APPROACH CLEARANCE AFTER THE FLIGHT CREW 
REPORTS THE RWY OR THE PRECEDING AIRCRAFT INSIGHT. 
2.4 AFTER RECEIVING THE VISUAL APPROACH CLEARANCE, THE ALTITUDE 
AND HEADING AT PILOT'S DISCRETION, THE FLIGHT CREW IS RESPONSIBLE 
FOR MAINTAINING SAFE SEPARATION BETWEEN THE AIRCRAFT AND 
 )

FOLLOW THE PRECEDING AIRCRAFT FOR APPROACH. AFTER RECEIVING THE 
VISUAL APPROACH FOLLOWING PRECEDING AIRCRAFT CLEARANCE, THE FLIGHT 
CREW IS RESPONSIBLE FOR MAINTAINING SAFE SEPARATION FROM THE 
PRECEDING AIRCRAFT. 
2.5 WHEN IMPLEMENT VISUAL APPROACH, PILOTS SHOULD COMPLY WITH THE 
FOLLOWING SPEED RESTRICTIONS UNTIL OTHERWISE INSTRUCTED. WHILE 
AIRCRAFT CONDUCTING RADAR VECTORING VISUAL APPROACH, IAS SHOULD BE 
180KT WHEN 8NM TO TOUCHDOWN, 160KT WHEN 6NM TO TOUCHDOWN ON FINAL. 
WHILE AIRCRAFT CONDUCTING A SHORT FINAL VISUAL APPROACH THE FLIGHT 
CREW SHALL CONTROL IAS NOT TO EXCEED 180 KNOTS WHEN COMMENCING THE 
VISUAL APPROACH, AND THE FLIGHT CREWSHOULD MAINTAIN IAS NOT LESS 
THAN 160KT DURING TURNING TO BASE. IF THE SPEED CANNOT BE 
MAINTAINED, THE FLIGHT CREW SHOULD INFORM ATC IN TIME. 
3. EMERGENCY PROCEDURES 
3.1 CONVERSION AND TERMINATION OF VISUAL APPROACH 
3.1.1 DURING A VISUAL APPROACH, IF THE PILOT LOSES VISUAL 
 ) 
// // REFERENCE (TO THE AERODROME OR THE PRECEDING AIRCRAFT), THE 
PILOT MUST IMMEDIATELY INFORM THE CONTROLLER OF THE SITUATION AND 
SUBSEQUENT INTENTIONS. THE CONTROLLER MAY THEN ASSIST THE AIRCRAFT 
IN CONVERTING TO ANOTHER VISUAL APPROACH, A PRECISION APPROACH, OR 
EXECUTING A MISSED APPROACH BASED ON THE PILOT'SINTENTIONS. 
3.1.2 FOR AN AIRCRAFT CONDUCTING A SHORT FINAL VISUAL APPROACH, IF 
VISUAL REFERENCE IS LOST OR THE APPROACH IS ABORTED FOR OTHER 
REASONS AFTER COMMENCING THE TURNING TO BASE, IN PRINCIPLE,THE 
PILOT FOLLOWS THE ESTABLISHED BASE AND FINAL DIRECTIONS TO JOIN 
THE RNAV ILS/DME Z MISSED APPROACH PROCEDURE OF LANDING RWY. 
3.1.3 FOR AN AIRCRAFT CONDUCTING RADAR VECTORING VISUAL APPROACH, 
THE PROCEDURE FOR ABORTING THE APPROACH IS THE SAME AS THE RNAV 
ILS/DME Z MISSED APPROACH PROCEDURE OF LANDING RWY. 
3.2 COMMUNICATION FAILURE 
3.2.1 IF LANDING CLEARANCE HAS BEEN RECEIVED PRIOR TO 
COMMUNICATION FAILURE, THE FLIGHT CREW MAY CONTINUE APPROACH AND 
LAND. 
3.2.2 
 )

UPON MUTUAL APPROVAL. ATC WILL INFORM THE CREW OF THE EXPECTED

2.3 AFTER RECEIVING THE VISUAL APPROACH CLEARANCE,THE ALTITUDE AND 
HEADING SHALL BE AT THE PILOT'S OWN DISCRETION.FLYING TOWARD THE 
LANDING AIRPORT OR FOLLOW THE PRECEDING AIRCRAFT FOR VISUAL 
APPROACH, THE PILOT IS RESPONSIBLE FOR MAINTAINING SAFETY 
SEPARATION BETWEEN PRECEDING AIRCRAFT AND GROUND OBSTACLES. 
2.4 HONGQIAO AIRPORT WILL BROADCAST THE VISUAL APPROACH 
INFORMATION ON THE ATIS. 
3. TERMINATION OF VISUAL 
 ) 
// // APPROACH 
3.1 THE ATC WILL PROACTIVELY TERMINATE THE VISUAL APPROACH WHEN 
PILOT REPORTS THAT IT IS UNABLE TO CONTINUE AND COMPLETE THE 
VISUAL APPROACH DUE TO WEATHER CONDITIONS OR OTHER REASONS. 
3.2 THE ATC WILL PROACTIVELY TERMINATE THE VISUAL APPROACH WHEN 
THE WEATHER CONDITIONS ARE BELOW THE METEOROLOGICAL STANDARDS FOR 
THE VISUAL APPROACH. 
3.3 THE ATC WILL PROACTIVELY TERMINATE THE VISUAL APPROACH WHEN 
DISCOVERS SITUATION THAT MAY AFFECT FLIGHT SAFETY DURING THE 
VISUAL APPROACH. 
3.4 WHEN THE AIRCRAFT IS UNABLE TO COMPLETE THE VISUAL APPROACH 
AND WILL CONVERT TO INSTRUMENT APPROACH OR TERMINATE THE APPROACH. 
THE ATC WILL PROVIDE NECESSARY ASSISTANCE AND ALLOCATE THE 
REQUIRED SEPARATION. 
3.5 AFTER TERMINATING THE VISUAL APPROACH, THE ATC WILL ISSUE 
HEADING OR ALTITUDE INSTRUCTIONS TO THE AIRCRAFT TO ESTABLISH THE 
SAFE SEPARATION AS SOON AS POSSIBLE. 
 )
